method: For each task, run the minimum chain of existing single-purpose MCP tools that answers it (the baseline), then run the new composite `orient` tool once. Compare round trips and raw response byte counts; check that `orient` returns the same node set the baseline returns. This measures round trips and bytes, not semantic probes: it does not re-verify whether the underlying graph edges (Calls, IsTest, impact) are themselves correct -- that is what core-representative-v1, typescript-support-v1, and go-support-v1 already gate. It only measures whether bundling those existing, separately-gated answers into one tool call is worth it.
motivation: The MCP server exposes six single-purpose tools (get_source, find_definition, search_code, ask_codebase, impacted_tests, review_changes; crates/aether-app/src/project/commands/mcp.rs:275-519). Answering 'what am I about to touch and what does it reach' for one starting node requires chaining several of them: get_source for the source, ask_codebase('what calls X?') and ask_codebase('what does X call?') for callers/callees (crates/aether-graph/src/knowledge.rs:25-28's Callers/Callees query shapes), impacted_tests for coverage, and ask_codebase('what would break if I change X?') for the impact set (knowledge.rs:23-24's Impact query shape, backed by aether-graph/src/impact.rs's impact_of). Every one of those calls is a separate subprocess round trip (mcp.rs:572-626, run_tool re-execs the girder binary per call). This policy states in advance what counts as a win for bundling them into one `orient` call.

baseline_tool_reference.ask_codebase_callers: arguments {"question": "what calls <path>?"} -> girder query <root> "what calls <path>?" (parse_query recognises the 'what calls X' / 'who calls X' / 'callers of X' shape, knowledge.rs:75-81)
baseline_tool_reference.ask_codebase_callees: arguments {"question": "what does <path> call?"} -> girder query <root> "what does <path> call?" (knowledge.rs:83-92)
baseline_tool_reference.ask_codebase_impact: arguments {"question": "what would break if I change <path>?"} -> girder query <root> "what would break if I change <path>?" (knowledge.rs:67-71)
baseline_tool_reference.search_code_for_intent: arguments {"query": <intent text>} -> girder search <root> <intent text>, used only when the task's starting point is a natural-language description rather than an exact path

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: Before changing dijkstra's signature or behavior, an engineer needs its source, who calls it (tests/graph.rs's dijk and test_astar_null_heuristic per core-representative-v1's dijkstra-cross-file-call and astar-test-dijkstra-call cases), what it calls, and which tests would need to be re-run.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::algo::dijkstra::dijkstra?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: from_slice delegates to from_trait and constructs a SliceRead (core-representative-v1's from-slice-wrapper and from-slice-nested-argument-call cases) -- an engineer touching it needs those callees plus its callers before changing the delegation.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::de::from_slice?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: The string-receiver Regex::replace must resolve to its own replacen, not the same-named bytes-module method (core-representative-v1's string-replace-owner and string-replace-not-bytes cases) -- exactly the owner-disambiguation an orienting engineer needs to see before editing.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::regex::string::Regex::replace?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: Command::invoke must resolve its Context receiver to Context::invoke and not to same-named Group::invoke or CliRunner::invoke (core-representative-v1's command-invoke-not-group / command-invoke-not-runner negative cases) -- an engineer needs to see exactly which invoke it calls before touching dispatch.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::click::core::Command::invoke?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: parse_args fans out into an options phase and an arguments phase (core-representative-v1's parser-options-phase / parser-arguments-phase cases) -- direct callees at depth 1 are exactly what an engineer needs before changing parse order.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::click::parser::_OptionParser::parse_args?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: generate_aliases invokes its own private _generate_alias helper (core-representative-v1's alias-generator-helper case) -- an engineer needs that callee and any callers before changing the public method's contract.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::pydantic::aliases::AliasGenerator::generate_aliases?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: get is a thin wrapper delegating to request (core-representative-v1's get-wrapper case) -- a low-fan-out case where an engineer mainly needs the one callee and the test coverage, not a large caller set.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::requests::api::get?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: prepare_request fans out to PreparedRequest::prepare, merge_setting, merge_hooks, merge_cookies, and cookiejar_from_dict (core-representative-v1's session-* cases) -- a high-fan-out case that stresses depth-1 callee reporting and the output cap.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::requests::sessions::Session::prepare_request?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: safeParse calls handleResult (typescript-support-v1's zod-safe-parse-calls-handle-result-style case) -- the first cross-language (TypeScript) task in this corpus.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::types::ZodType::safeParse?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: MergeDeep is a pure type-level construct (typescript-support-v1's module-contains-* cases for this file are Contains edges, not Calls) -- deliberately adversarial: a competent engineer here needs to confirm there ARE no runtime callers/callees/tests, not receive a large fan-out.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::source::merge-deep::MergeDeep?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: Afero::ReadFile calls the package-level ReadFile function (go-support-v1's afero-readfile-calls case) -- the first Go task in this corpus.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::Afero::ReadFile?

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: Conn::WriteJSON calls Conn::NextWriter (go-support-v1's conn-writejson-calls-nextwriter-style case) -- a second Go task exercising method-receiver call resolution.

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::Conn::WriteJSON?

starting_point.value: compute the shortest path between two nodes

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: The intended resolution is crate::algo::dijkstra::dijkstra. description-search-accuracy-v1 measured 41.9% top-1 / 77.4% top-5 for this kind of description-to-symbol search, so this task is expected to be adversarial: it is included specifically to record whether orient's intent path fails the same way get_source's does, not to inflate the corpus's pass rate.

arguments.query: compute the shortest path between two nodes

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::algo::dijkstra::dijkstra?

starting_point.value: read a file from the in-memory filesystem

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: The intended resolution is crate::Afero::ReadFile or a node in crate::mem. Adversarial: afero's naming (Afero, mem::File) is generic enough that description search plausibly resolves to an unrelated same-named helper elsewhere in the graph -- recorded honestly either way.

arguments.query: read a file from the in-memory filesystem

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::Afero::ReadFile?

starting_point.value: serialize a value to a JSON string

corpus.what_a_competent_engineer_needs: The intended resolution is crate::ser::to_string (core-representative-v1's to-string-macro-call case names it directly). Adversarial: to_string_pretty is an equally plausible top-1 for this phrasing, so a 'wrong but related' resolution is a realistic failure mode to record, distinct from a nonsense resolution.

arguments.query: serialize a value to a JSON string

arguments.question: what would break if I change crate::ser::to_string?

threshold.byte_ratio_rationale: orient's response is a union of what the baseline's 5-6 separate calls return (source, callers, callees, tests, impact), so its content is expected to be close to the sum of those payloads; the 1.2 ceiling allows for orient's own envelope (semantic paths, confidence/truncation fields) while still requiring that bundling into one exchange not come at more than a 20% byte premium. If a task exceeds 1.2, that is recorded as FAILED for that task, not smoothed into an aggregate -- round-trip reduction alone does not justify an unbounded byte cost.
threshold.round_trip_rationale: The whole point of `orient` is one exchange instead of the baseline's 5 (symbol tasks) or 6 (intent tasks) round trips. A composite that itself needs more than one call is not a composite.

correctness.requirement: For every task, the union of node paths orient returns (target, callers, callees, tests, impact set) must equal the union of node paths the baseline's chained calls return, restricted to whatever depth/cap orient actually reports (a deliberate, disclosed truncation is not a correctness failure; a silent omission is).
correctness.rationale: orient must not be a lossy shortcut. It is allowed to say less than the baseline only when it says so explicitly (truncation counts and paths, or a stated confidence caveat for intent tasks).

reported_but_not_gated: whether an intent task's top-1 resolution matches the task's stated intended symbol (tracked for the record, per docs/description-search-accuracy-policy.json's precedent of leaving search-accuracy weaknesses visible rather than excluding them)
byte ratio for the two Go-corpus tasks specifically, since go-support-v1's own observation recorded a missed Calls edge (a function-value reference) and this measurement does not re-verify that fix
